title: The Mexica Foundation Omen
subtitle: An origin tradition for the city of Mexico

learningObjectives.text: Why does the city rise on a lake?

omen.author: Lewis Spence
omen.locator: Chapter I · THE CIVILISATION OF MEXICO; Chapter I · THE CIVILISATION OF MEXICO, normalized characters 46465-47015
omen.excerpt: The most popular of these relates how the nomadic Nahua beheld perched upon a cactus plant an eagle of great size and majesty, grasping in its talons a huge serpent, and spreading its wings to catch the rays of the rising sun. The soothsayers or medicine-men of the tribe, reading a good omen in the spectacle, advised the leaders of the people to settle on the spot, and, hearkening to the voice of what they considered divine authority, they proceeded to drive piles into the marshy ground, and thus laid the foundation of the great city of Mexico.
omen.note: Verbatim prose from Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century synthesis, not a direct translation of the Indigenous source material he discusses. Preserve its dated, colonial framing.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wandering for a sign
narrativeBlocks.body: The Mexica wander for generations, driven from place to place, carrying a prophecy: where you see an eagle perched on a cactus devouring a serpent, there build your city.

narrativeBlocks.title: The lake nobody wanted
narrativeBlocks.body: When priests finally see the sign, it is on a tiny island in Lake Texcoco — land the valley's powers had already written off as worthless.

narrativeBlocks.title: A city built on water
narrativeBlocks.body: They build Tenochtitlan in the lake itself: canals for streets, causeways for roads, floating chinampa gardens feeding the people — a Venice of the Americas.

narrativeBlocks.title: The sign on a flag
narrativeBlocks.body: The eagle on the cactus is on Mexico's flag today — a prophecy that became a founding image and then a national symbol.

narrativeBlocks.title: A Nahua charter myth
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a Mexica (one Nahua people) charter story: the sign legitimizes their right to rule the valley — prophecy as a deed of ownership.

quiz.prompt: What is the Mexica foundation omen?

choices.text: A jaguar on a temple stone
An eagle perched on a cactus devouring a serpent — the sign for where to build
The sun rising through a pyramid

quiz.explanation: The eagle-and-serpent is the image on Mexico's flag today.

quiz.prompt: Why is Tenochtitlan built on a lake?

choices.text: The sign appeared on a lake island — land the powerful had rejected — so they built on water
The lake was sacred to Huitzilopochtli
They were driven there by enemies

quiz.explanation: The prophecy made the worthless land the chosen place.
